sanjay: quick proposal — switch admission control to a "soft-window" degrade + probabilistic queue during short spikes instead of immediate rejects. the aim: keep tail latency bounded but avoid 5xx spikes and unhappy app teams.

julia: high level — how is soft-window different from our current 'staged-shedding' experiments?

sanjay: current staged-shedding tends to drop requests once queue depth > X. soft-window instead allows a short time-window (e.g., 1–3s) where we accept and degrade (lower tokens or fallback model) and then probabilistically queue remaining requests. so fewer hard rejects, but controlled cost.

maria: can we get a config snippet? want to show infra/ops what they'd toggle.

sanjay: sure — rough draft: ```yaml
admit_policy:
  mode: soft-window
  window_ms: 2000
  degrade_rate: 0.3   # fraction of requests to serve with cheaper model or truncate
  queue_prob_threshold: 0.75  # when load metric normalized > this, apply probabilistic queueing
  per_tenant_override: true
```

eli: interesting. questions: 1) per-tenant SLAs — how do we respect committed QPS? 2) what about model-specific costs (e.g., Llama3 70B vs small)?

sanjay: per-tenant: admit check still honors reserved capacity buckets first. soft-window only applies to best-effort tiers. for model-specific we add model_cost_multiplier to degrade_score so bigger models get higher degrade probability or forced fallback.

cheng: what metrics do we watch during canary? p95 latency, reject-rate, cost delta, and dropped tokens. also want percentage of 'degraded' responses that fail quality checks (eval harness).

maria: would prefer explicit rollout knobs: region, pool, and a per-service cap. e.g., canary only in eu-west-1 pool-3 for 2 hours, 1% global traffic.

sanjay: agreed. proposed canary plan in PR: - region: eu-west-1 - pool: pool-3 (g4dn-like) - window: 2s - degrade: small-model fallback - traffic: route 5% from best-effort to policy for 3 hours.

eli: we should simulate cost impact first. ran a quick micro-sim on last week's traffic slices: median token-cost drop ~6% but p95 latency improved ~120ms; reject-rate down from 0.9% to 0.15% on peak windows. feasibility looks good.

julia: nice. any risk to emergency queues/backpressure cascading to other regions?

sanjay: risk: probabilistic queueing could increase simultaneous waiting requests across pools. mitigation: window length capped, and global admission controller will throttle probability if global inflight > threshold. also we enforce per-region max-waiters.

cheng: can we see the controller logic? pseudo: ```python
if load_metric > threshold:
  if rand() < queue_prob(load_metric):
    enqueue(request, max_wait=window_ms)
  else:
    serve_degraded(request)
else:
  serve_normal(request)
```

ops-bot: deploy triggered: admit-controller/v2 -> canary on eu-west-1 pool-3 (sha: ab12cd34).

maria: who owns the experiment dashboard? need p95 latency by tenant, reject-rate, degraded-rate, and cost-per-token delta.

eli: i'll wire a grafana panel and add a short-run smoke test to check model fallback correctness.

julia: one more ask: add a flag to force hard-reject fallback when memory pressure is high (OOM risk) — we do not want queues to blow up GPU memory/caches.

sanjay: yes — config will include emergency_mode: hard_reject_on_oom=true.

cheng: timeline? if canary is green, roll to us-east-1 low traffic pools next day?

sanjay: proposal: canary 3h + 1h validation window. if metrics pass (<0.2% increase in error-rate, reject-rate <0.3%, cost delta <8%), roll to a handful of low-priority pools in us-east-1.

maria: ping @product for communication to customers about transient degraded responses and fallback models. need a short blurb for status page in case of perceived quality regression.

eli: note for runbook: when degrade_rate spikes above expected, revert: set mode=reject-only. quick CLI to revert will be added to ops playbook.

julia: :thumbsup: OK — please open PR with config + canary playbook + grafana dashboards. assign to me for review.

ops-bot: canary started (eu-west-1 pool-3) at 2023-11-02T15:12:10Z. monitoring hooks created.

sanjay: thanks all — I'll open PR and drop links here. keeping this thread for rollout notes.
